# Operator scientific notes

This is an author-developed numerical world, followed by independent same-family
provisional review and a separately recorded experimental-integration phase.
Its purpose is controlled investigation of terminal frequency response. It does
not represent a validated instrument, unique internal topology recovery,
contamination resistance, autonomous discovery or calibrated task difficulty.

## Physical convention and construction

The public sinusoid convention is `Re(V exp(+i omega t))`, with peak source
amplitude. A resistor, capacitor and inductor have impedances `R`, `1/(i omega C)`
and `i omega L`. KCL at the measured terminal gives

```
Y_box = 1/R_leak + sum_j 1/(R_j + i omega L_j + 1/(i omega C_j))
V_port / V_source = 1 / (1 + R_source * (1/R_load + Y_box)).
```

These are the independent reference equations, not the production kernel's
implementation. MIT's official [driven-RLC teaching summary](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/8-02-physics-ii-electricity-and-magnetism-spring-2007/e9407519c0b6b8cbbc35ea4184efd62e_summary_w12d2.pdf)
sets out phasors, inductive/capacitive reactance, phase and series resonance.
The official [6.071J lecture sequence](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/6-071j-introduction-to-electronics-signals-and-measurement-spring-2006/pages/lecture-notes/)
provides the KCL/nodal, impedance, sinusoidal steady-state and transient circuit
background. The finite construction and derivations below are specific to this
prototype; the citations do not validate its implementation or calibration.

All devices have a positive leakage resistor in parallel with one of three
private branch constructions:

| Operator structure | Dynamic states | Random component values |
| --- | --- | --- |
| One series RC branch | Capacitor voltage | Leakage R, branch R and C |
| Two series RC branches in parallel | Two capacitor voltages | Leakage R, two R and two C |
| One series RLC branch | Capacitor voltage and inductor current | Leakage R, branch R, C and L |

Every sampled resistance, capacitance and inductance is positive. Generation
uses separate stable hash streams for the structure, parameters, panels and
measurement noise. It does not condition on response, baseline score or task
success. The two-RC sampled ranges favor separated relaxation scales. A distinct
explicit equivalence fixture lies within the broader allowed kernel domain and
need not be generated by that particular sampling policy.

## Independent state-space derivation

For RC branches let `g_j=1/R_j`, `G=1/R_source+1/R_load+1/R_leak+sum(g_j)`,
`d=1/(R_source G)` and `c_j=g_j/G`. KCL eliminates the port voltage:
`v=d u+c^T x`, where `x_j` is capacitor voltage. The state equations are

```
E = diag(C_j)
F_jk = g_j (c_k - delta_jk)
B_j = g_j d
E x_dot = F x + B u,       v = c^T x + d u.
```

For one RLC branch use `G=1/R_source+1/R_load+1/R_leak`, `d=1/(R_source G)`
and states `x=(v_C,i_L)`. Then

```
E = diag(C, L)
F = [[0, 1], [-1, -(R + 1/G)]]
B = [0, d],      c = [0, -1/G],      v = c x + d u.
```

For each positive frequency the production kernel solves
`(i omega E - F) x = B` and obtains unit-source gain `d+c x`. Multiplication
by the specified source amplitude gives the measured phasor. This is the exact
finite-dimensional frequency equation evaluated in float64, with no time step,
frequency interpolation or numerical integration. It is not exact arithmetic.
The descriptor row scaling preserves conditioning as a positive L approaches
zero; the zero-L branch uses the RC equations. This conditioning decision was
recorded before any response calculation. A zero-branch resistor limit is an
explicit validation fixture and is not sampled as a fourth private structure.

For zero source, stored energy is `sum(C_j v_Cj^2/2)` for RC branches or
`C v_C^2/2+L i_L^2/2` for RLC. Its derivative is
`-(1/R_source+1/R_load+1/R_leak) v^2 - sum(R_j i_j^2)`.
The only invariant state with zero dissipation is the origin. This establishes
asymptotic stability for these positive-component networks; an RLC energy
derivative need not be strictly negative at every nonzero instantaneous state.
Explicit generalized-eigenvalue checks cover all three structures at the fixed
development seeds and extreme source/load settings.

The reference admittance has positive real part. Consequently the measured
terminal gain has magnitude at most one. This bound is for the chosen terminal
voltage: an internal reactive component's voltage need not share it. Real system
coefficients imply conjugate symmetry between positive and negative frequencies;
the public instrument only accepts positive frequencies. RC quadrature signs
and the possible inductive sign change follow from the stated phasor convention.

## What the ambiguity examples establish

Use leakage 5000 ohm, branch resistance 250 ohm and an RC capacitance of 2 uF.
At `f0=100 Hz`, construct a series RLC branch with `L=0.08 H` and

```
1/C_RLC = 1/C_RC + (2 pi f0)^2 L.
```

The branch reactances, and hence the complete port impedances, agree at f0.
For the predeclared 99.9, 100 and 100.1 Hz measurements, the largest computed
quadrature difference is 3.1919e-5 V. The full six-dimensional difference vector
has norm only 0.04581 times the 0.001 V noise SD per quadrature. This describes
weak information in one narrow sweep; it is not a hypothesis-test result and
does not imply equality over a nonzero interval. Unlimited repetitions can
resolve a nonzero discrepancy.

The predeclared 2–5000 Hz sweep separates these same fixed accounts: largest
difference 0.48586 V, RMS difference 0.18839 V across quadrature cells. No model
was refitted after observing the broader spectrum. Changing source/load at
exactly f0 retains equality (observed difference 6.94e-18 V). An external
resistive load cannot distinguish two devices with the same port impedance
at that frequency. Loading changes sensitivity and measurement conditioning,
not the information contained in exact terminal impedance.

There is also a stronger all-frequency limitation. Two parallel series-RC
branches `(2R,C/2)` have individual impedance twice that of `(R,C)`, so their
combined admittance equals the single branch exactly. With the same leakage,
all legal frequencies, amplitudes, source resistances and loads remain
indistinguishable. The broad-sweep numerical difference was 1.11e-16 V. This
identity is a derivation, not an inference that every similar-looking pair
is equivalent or that a sampled class can be recovered uniquely.

## Development evidence and limits

The predeclared four-instance development set realized zero single-RC, three
double-RC and one RLC device. The single-RC coverage gap is retained, without
remapping or replacement. The test fixtures cover that construction numerically;
they do not supply a missing empirical baseline cohort. Numerical/reference
agreement on fresh development spectra reached a maximum absolute difference
of 2.22e-16 V. Forty tests passed, including explicit parameter corners,
subnormal positive L, 1/65 rows, grid invariance, passivity, amplitude linearity,
invalid/huge/nonfinite inputs, noise reproducibility, work and failure limits,
public-description invariance and a public-record-only baseline isolation check.

There were 16 planned and 16 completed fresh queries and no unexpected failures.
Three intentional numerical failures are retained in the private event log.
Source histories contain three noisy spectra per instance; query targets are
clean and private. Source and query specs are distinct. The weak comparator
chooses a nearest apparatus record, interpolates its gain in log frequency,
and clamps extrapolation to endpoint values. It neither estimates an impedance
nor corrects the source/load mismatch using hidden equations. Its data-dependent
improvement is not a strong authored reference or an agent result.

Public controls are informative enough to explore multiple frequency scales,
but no campaign has established a useful autonomous research budget. The finite
band, finite noise, ideal component assumptions, only three generated structure
families, unbalanced development set and absence of transient observations limit
all claims. No full-topology, complete-law, contamination or discovery-depth
claim follows from these checks.

## Experimental integration following review

The frozen independent review concluded A/B supported within their bounded scope
and C not ready because shared adapters were missing. The implementation phase
then added experimental registration, five full-description task profiles,
explicit frequency claim/readout semantics, the independent unbounded Gaussian
observation contract with zero bias, no assigned-initial-state calibration, and
public evidence spec/axis allowlists. The original review, hashes and failures
remain unchanged; implementation checks are separate evidence.

Frequency rows are not elapsed time. Both paired-claim arms must contain 1–65
strictly increasing legal frequencies. The same row index/channel is read in each
arm, and frequencies may differ for a spectral contrast. A source/load contrast
that also changes frequency is combined, not an isolated apparatus effect.
There is no t=0 assignment, carried state or temporal lag. Eligibility does not
certify novelty or internal mechanism identification. Public amplitude scaling
and known external transformations still require no unknown device explanation.

Fresh observations use unique operator-generated keys; clean and replay paths
are not candidate capabilities. Full-description publication withholds internal
structures, component ranges, private seeds and parameters. The separate
apparatus_only variant remains fail-closed. The prospective schema permits an
unobserved frequency for mechanism discrimination; its unchanged regime-transfer
gate requires a changed non-axis control. Integration does not expand historical
cohorts or the seven-world audited null bank, change old score formulas, fill the
single-RC empirical calibration gap, or establish model capability or task
scientific difficulty.
